sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Statutory Origin**: Established in **1992** through an amendment to the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** (Chapter IV-A).
• **Administrative Control**: It functions under the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)**.
• **Core Mandate**: To enforce **Recognition of Zoo Rules, 2009**, ensuring scientific management, veterinary care, and education.
• **Key Metric**: Every zoo in India must obtain **compulsory recognition** from the CZA to operate legally.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Chaired by MoEFCC Minister; 10 members + Member Secretary
Prelims: Composition of bodies is a favorite trap

items.definition: Conservation of species outside their natural habitats (zoos, botanical gardens, gene banks). CZA is the nodal agency for zoo-based ex-situ efforts.
The legal framework defining standards for housing, upkeep, veterinary care, and education in zoos. Non-compliance leads to de-recognition.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Conservation Breeding**: Targeted programs for critically endangered species (e.g., Red Panda, Vulture, Great Indian Bustard).
• **Zoo Management**: Standardizing animal exchange programs and health monitoring protocols.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Inadequate funding for smaller municipal zoos, human-animal conflict in urban fringes, and ethical concerns regarding captivity.
• **Solutions**: Digital health monitoring, public-private partnerships for zoo modernization, and focus on 'Rescue Centers'.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'CZA-RE'
• **Decoded Meaning**: C (Conservation Breeding), Z (Zoo Recognition), A (Animal Welfare), R (Research), E (Education).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: CZA is NOT a constitutional body; it is a statutory body. It does not manage National Parks or Wildlife Sanctuaries (which are under the State/National Board for Wildlife).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Ex-situ conservation synergy' when discussing how CZA complements the 'In-situ' efforts of the National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA).

keyTakeaways: CZA is a statutory body under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
It regulates all zoos in India; recognition is mandatory for operation.
Its primary focus is ex-situ conservation and scientific management of captive wildlife.
